title: Bug summary — a multi-site, multi-page roll-up of known issues
description: The machine contract behind the Bug-Summary document (QA-Documentation/Custom-Reports/Bug-Summary). One file = one edition of the roll-up. It does NOT replace bug.schema.json: a bug RECORD (repro, expected, actual, evidence) is owned by Bug-Reports; this file is the REPORT that counts those bugs per page and per site. A row here may be sourced from a kit bug record (bugId), from someone else's tracker (trackerRef), or imported from a legacy sheet — but every row must say WHERE it came from, and every row must carry a status, because a roll-up whose rows have no status cannot answer the only question it is opened for: what is still broken?

summaryId.description: BS-<YYYY-MM-DD>[-slug]. One edition of the roll-up, dated. A summary with no date cannot be compared to the next one.

generatedAt.description: When this edition was produced. Counts age: a roll-up read six weeks later is a historical document, not a status.

environment.description: The build / environment the issues were found on (e.g. 'staging 2024-01-24'). Two editions taken on different environments are not comparable — the same rule as PageSpeed rounds.

source.description: Where the rows came from. Required, and it is the honesty anchor of the whole document: an imported roll-up must never present itself as a measured one.

kind.description: kit-bug-records = rolled up from BUG-NNN JSONs (bug.schema.json). tracker-export = pulled from Redmine/Jira. imported-sheet = read out of an existing spreadsheet (the source document is READ-ONLY; the importer must never write back to it). manual = typed by a human, which means the counts are only as true as the typing.

ref.description: Path, spreadsheet id, or tracker query the rows came from.

severityScale.description: The severity vocabulary of THIS engagement, ordered most severe first (e.g. ['Critical','Major','Minor','Trivial']). It is a flat array on purpose: it drives the geometry of the Sheet (one counter column per value), exactly as PLATFORMS drives the checklist. Clients bring their own scale; the kit reproduces it rather than silently remapping it. Counts from two editions with different scales are not comparable.

severityMap.description: Optional mapping from this engagement's scale to the kit's canonical bug.schema.json severities (Critical|Major|Medium|Low|High|Info). Required in practice whenever rows are sourced from kit bug records, so the roll-up and the bug records cannot drift apart.

sites.description: The sites (or apps, or products) the roll-up spans. One site = one band in the Sheet. A single-site roll-up is just a roll-up with one site — the document does not change shape.

pages.description: The MODULES the bugs are grouped by — a module, page, screen or feature area, whatever this engagement groups by (the owner's sheet calls its grand total 'All modules' while naming each band after a page). One module = one collapsible band with its own severity counters.

issues.description: May be empty: a page that was tested and came back clean is a RESULT, and it belongs in the document. An empty page band and an absent page band say different things.

id.description: A STABLE id, unique across the whole summary (e.g. 'consumer-landing-07'). The per-page ordinal in the Sheet's № column restarts at 1 on every page and therefore cannot address a row: any derived view (Left issues) that carries no stable id cannot be traced back to its source row — which is exactly how the reference document's second tab drifted from its first.

bugId.description: The kit bug record this row rolls up (bug.schema.json). Present whenever source.kind = kit-bug-records.

trackerRef.description: Issue key/URL in the owner's tracker (e.g. a Redmine id) when the bug lives outside the kit.

summary.description: One line, as it reads in the Sheet. Not a bug report — the report lives in the bug record.

severity.description: MUST be one of severityScale. Enforced by validate.mjs, not by this schema alone: a severity outside the scale is counted by no column and disappears from every total — a silently lost bug.

status.description: OPTIONAL — only for a summary that is being WORKED. A retrospective roll-up of a CLOSED engagement reports what was FOUND; it does not track state, and inventing a status column for it would be the kit redesigning the owner's document instead of reproducing it. When present it drives the optional Status column and the derived Left-issues view (BS_STATUS_COLUMN=1). Values: the six bug.schema.json lifecycle states plus three a roll-up needs and a record does not — 'unknown' (the source states none; counted as still owed, never assumed fixed), 'not-verified' (not re-checked this edition; the debt stands), 'reassigned' (accepted as an improvement, no longer a defect). ONLY 'verified' means proven fixed: 'fixed' means a developer said so.

notes.description: Free text: the REASONING behind the status. It must never be the only place the status is recorded — prose is invisible to a counter.

evidence.description: Screenshots / recordings. A row with no evidence is an observation, not a demonstrated defect (Test-Oracles: no oracle, no verdict) — the builder flags it rather than dropping it.

hostRisk.description: Evidence rots. Link hosts that expire or require an account (screencast.com, prnt.sc, personal Dropbox links) lose the proof and take the bug's provability with them — the same lesson as PageSpeed's 30-day shareable links. The builder marks these; durable evidence is re-hosted per the workspace's file-hosting rule.

foundOn.description: Optional: device/browser/resolution the issue was found on.

severitySource.description: WHERE THE SEVERITY CAME FROM — and it matters more here than anywhere else in the kit, because the tracker these rows come from has NO severity field: a human assigns it, or an agent proposes it. 'owner' = a human triaged it. 'tracker' = the source system recorded it. 'agent-proposed' = an agent derived it from the severity decision tree (BUG_REPORTS_RULES.md) and it is a HYPOTHESIS, not a triage decision. Every statistic in the document is built out of these values, so a machine's guess must never be able to pass as a human's judgement: the builder notes every proposed cell with the branch that produced it, notes the count on the Severity header, and says it out loud on every build. The same discipline as bug.schema.json's `priorityProposed`, and the same rule as Test-Oracles: a verdict with no oracle behind it is not a verdict.

severityRationale.description: Required in practice when severitySource is 'agent-proposed': the branch of the severity decision tree that produced it (e.g. 'core flow blocked, no workaround → Major'). A proposed severity with no stated reasoning cannot be reviewed, and an unreviewable hypothesis counted as a fact is exactly what this field exists to prevent.

moduleSource.description: HOW this row got its module — and it matters for the same reason severitySource does: a module read off the board is a FACT; a module inferred from the bug's own wording is an INFERENCE, and every per-module count is built out of it. 'container' = the issue that holds it names the module. 'parent' = the parent task does. 'subject' = the issue's own subject IS a place. 'record' = a bug RECORD (bug.schema.json) declared it in its `component` field — a human-authored field on the record itself, so it is a fact about the record rather than something a tool read out of prose; this is what bs-from-bugs.mjs emits. 'owner-mapped' = a human said so in MODULE_MAP (the strongest). 'summary-inferred' = the tool read a place out of the bug's summary text ("The Notifications screen shows hardcoded mock data") — used ONLY when the text names exactly ONE place; two or more ("on the Library and Story screens") is ambiguous and the bug stays unplaced rather than being filed under a coin-flip. 'agent-placed' = an AGENT read the bug and decided where it belongs — a judgement, weaker than the board's own words and stronger than nothing, and it is recorded as such so a reader can tell it apart from a fact. 'unplaced' = nothing said where it lives, so it sits in General.

unplaced.description: TRUE marks the band that holds the bugs the source could NOT place — conventionally named "General". It is a DEBT, not a module: it means the bugs were found but nobody can say where they live. Two rules follow from it and the builder enforces both: the band is rendered LAST within its site (a debt belongs at the end of the list, not interleaved with real modules), and it is scoped to ITS OWN SITE — a document covering several sites gets one General per site, never a shared bucket, because merging the unplaced bugs of two different products into one band would invent a relationship that does not exist. Dropping these bugs instead is NOT the honest alternative: it under-reports the grand total, which is the one number this document exists to produce.
